clue.text: Preserve in case it is completely full

parts.note: a preserve is fruit conserve, such as jam
goods put in a case or box are packed

explanation.surface: Advice to store fruit conserve in a case to check whether it is full.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crammed so tight it can hold no more is said to be stuffed to the brim, an informal compound.

clue.text: Generally accepted truth of a team award

parts.note: XI is the Roman eleven, a cricket or football team
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone states a self-evident fact about a team receiving an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour given by the monarch; XI stands for a side of eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident principle accepted without proof is a maxim or postulate.

clue.text: A cur turned up following father to temple

indicators.note: the letters for the dog come after those for father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue the words a cur are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A mongrel dog trails behind a man as he walks to a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the letters for 'A cur', which in a down entry reads upwards; 'following' places them after the word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine is a kind of temple.

clue.text: Stick his eminence in the centre

indicators.note: the letters for his eminence are placed within those for the centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
HE is the abbreviation for His Eminence, a cardinal's title

explanation.surface: An instruction to place a cardinal right in the middle of things.
explanation.walkthrough: His Eminence is the formal title of a Roman Catholic cardinal, abbreviated in crosswords to its two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together is to adhere or hold firmly as one mass.

clue.text: Two pairs of braces

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so two pairs of braces is two times two times two items

explanation.surface: Someone buys two sets of trouser suspenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Braces look like trouser suspenders, but a brace is a pair (of game birds, say): two braces make four, and two pairs of them make twice that.
explanation.definitionFit: Two times two pairs gives the number after seven, which counts this many items.

clue.text: Red-faced athlete found in the garden

parts.note: someone red-faced is flushed scarlet
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: An embarrassed or flushed sprinter turns up among the garden flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: this climbing bean, with red flowers, is grown in many vegetable plots.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing bean with red flowers is a common vegetable plant grown in plots and allotments.

clue.text: Initial communication from Tashkent?

parts.note: an initial is the large first character of a word, and a message sent from Tashkent comes from Uzbekistan's chief city

explanation.surface: Someone receives their first message from the Uzbek city of Tashkent.
explanation.walkthrough: Tashkent is the seat of government of Uzbekistan, so mail posted there comes from the nation's chief city; 'Initial' also means an upper-case first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper-case character, such as the one opening a sentence, is printed large at the start.

clue.text: Silly way nanny is behaving?

parts.note: a nanny is a female goat, so a nanny behaving naturally behaves like her own animal kind

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the children's nurse is behaving foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny' suggests a children's nurse, but a nanny is also a female goat; the phrase is British slang for fooling about.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fooling around or behaving in a foolish, clownish way.

clue.text: Slander when I appear in character

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the letter I is placed within the word for a character

parts.note: a character in a story is a person

explanation.surface: Someone is defamed for making an appearance in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear in' looks like part of the surface's stage picture but is the container signal; 'when' gives a two-letter conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: A damaging remark attacking someone's reputation is a slur or calumny.

clue.text: Eg central revolving shape

indicators.note: the letters of eg central spin round into a new order

explanation.surface: An example of a figure rotating about its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' scrambles EG and CENTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with four right angles is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Small crowd go away hastily

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
to crowd a space is to cram it

explanation.surface: A little gathering of people is told to leave quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang order means clear off or leave at once.

clue.text: Short tour be made by clan

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a tour is a trip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family group goes on a brief excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts TRIP to TRI; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a family group or social community sharing ancestry.

clue.text: Biscuit contained iron but not in peace-time

indicators.note: the letters for war hold the symbol for iron within them

parts.note: conflict that happens only when there is no peace is war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A ration biscuit with iron content was issued only in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: FE, the chemical symbol for iron, goes inside WAR, described as what occurs except in times of peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp sweet cracker is a kind of light biscuit.

clue.text: Fought a pay war?

parts.note: one sense is carried on a war, the other is paid a regular salary, punning on the word for earnings

explanation.surface: A question about whether workers struggled in a dispute over salaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Armies carry on hostilities, so they are said to do this to a war; the same word also describes a worker who earns a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a campaign of fighting is the verb's past sense; employees earning salaries are described with the same word.

clue.text: Obese person so rich to begin with

indicators.note: the word for rich goes first, before so

parts.note: rich food is fatty, so rich can mean fat

explanation.surface: A remark that a heavy person was wealthy from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulting nickname for a very overweight person, like 'fatty'.

clue.text: Anger management required in mountains

indicators.note: managing the letters of anger means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone needs to control their temper while up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'management' rearranges ANGER; 'required in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of peaks is called a mountain chain or sierra.

clue.text: Turn out article on volcanic matter

indicators.note: in an across clue the article sits on, or after, the first word

parts.note: to turn someone out is to eject them
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a piece about lava and ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' suggests producing an article, as a writer does; here it means expel.
explanation.definitionFit: Material thrown out of an erupting volcano, such as ash and rock, is the Latin plural for things cast out.

clue.text: Where cobbler works in the end

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker works at a foot-shaped form, so he works at that form
means finally, after a long wait

explanation.surface: A shoe-repairer finally finds his workbench.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block on which a shoemaker shapes and mends shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler works at his foot-shaped block, and the same phrase means finally, eventually.

clue.text: Fare provided by board

definitions.meaning: to fare is to manage or progress, as in 'how are you faring?'
to board a bus or train is to climb aboard it

explanation.surface: A passenger's ticket price is covered by the transport company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price and 'board' a company's directors, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or progress is one sense of the phrasal verb; to climb aboard a vehicle is the other.

clue.text: Knock everybody out

definitions.meaning: to knock is to hit or deliver a blow
the union cry calling all workers to stop work

explanation.surface: An instruction to render every person unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everybody out!' is the shop steward's call for a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit is one sense; a stoppage of work by all employees in a dispute is the other.

clue.text: Measure everything in turn before noon

indicators.note: this group comes ahead of the letter for noon
the letters for everything are placed within those for turn

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
all means everything

explanation.surface: An instruction to measure every item in rotation before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'before' the charade order; 'turn' in the surface suggests rotation, but here it is a go in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of liquid volume, eight pints, is a measure.

clue.text: Hit ball into crowd

definitions.meaning: in golf or cricket, to strike the ball hard forwards
a herd or throng, as of cattle being driven

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a ball into the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A past tense for striking a long shot is one sense; a large moving herd or mass of people is the other.

clue.text: Lapel back unfinished

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its final letter

parts.note: to back a car is to reverse it

explanation.surface: A lapel at the back of a jacket is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of REVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The turned-back edge of a coat, showing its underside, is a borrowed French tailoring term.

clue.text: Wrecker Virginia destroyed land

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state Virginia

indicators.note: the letters of land are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A destructive person ruined the land in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' is the anagram signal, rearranging the four letters of 'land' after the postal code for the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately damages property is a hooligan or wrecker.

clue.text: He or she has to be one

definitions.text: He or she has to be one

parts.words: He or she has to be one
parts.note: anyone who has something is by definition its possessor

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain person is obliged to be someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' looks like 'must', but read literally 'has' means possesses: a person who has a thing is its possessor.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor or proprietor is anyone who holds property.

clue.text: Proportion that is less than full share

indicators.note: a word less than full is missing its final letter

parts.note: a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their portion was smaller than a complete one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than full' drops the last letter of RATION; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation between two quantities expressed as a quotient is a proportion.

clue.text: Silver came across Capone

parts.note: to meet someone is to come across them
Al Capone was a Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster encountered a hoard of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is defined by example: it is one of the elements of this class.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is an example of a lustrous element such as gold, copper or iron.

clue.text: Two who are relatively close to craftsman

parts.note: ma is a mother, a close relative
a son is a close relative of his parent

explanation.surface: A pair of near relatives works alongside a skilled tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively close' means closely related: a mother and her boy are two close kin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker or bricklayer is a skilled tradesman who builds with stone.

clue.text: Get down cleaning with it?

parts.note: down is soft plumage, so a cleaning tool made of plumes gets down to the job

explanation.surface: A suggestion to kneel and scrub with a cleaning implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' suggests kneeling, but down here is fine soft plumage: this cleaning tool is made from bird plumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning tool made of bird plumes on a stick, for brushing dust off shelves.

clue.text: Seaside railway?

parts.note: a seaside is the shore, and a railway is a track or route, so a track along the shore

explanation.surface: A question about a train line running along the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railway' plays on a rail route, but the answer is the outline of the land where it meets the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The outline of the shore, where land meets sea, is the edge of a country's map.
